title: Sunday Special: An Episode of ‘The Coldest Case in Laramie’

sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我要测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的队伍。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界，并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，获取 nytimes.com/subscribe 上的特别优惠。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Michael.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是迈克尔。

sentences.en: Today, we here at The Daily wanted to share an excerpt from a new podcast series from NYT Audio and Serial.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们《每日新闻》团队想分享一段来自《纽约时报》音频和 Serial 制作的新播客系列的节选。

sentences.en: It's called The Coldest Case in Laramie.
sentences.zh: 它叫《拉勒米最冷悬案》。

sentences.en: And it's hosted by my colleague, investigative reporter Kim Barker.
sentences.zh: 由我的同事，调查记者金·巴克主持。

sentences.en: In it, Kim revisits an unsolved murder that took place while she was in high school in Laramie, Wyoming, nearly 40 years ago.
sentences.zh: 在节目中，金重访了一起未解谋杀案，案发时她还在怀俄明州拉勒米读高中，那是近40年前的事了。

sentences.en: A case that seemed to break wide open a few years ago with the arrest of a local police officer.
sentences.zh: 几年前，随着一名当地警官的被捕，这起案件似乎有了重大突破。

sentences.en: The evidence against the officer seemed strong.
sentences.zh: 针对该警官的证据看起来很充分。

sentences.en: But then, prosecutors abruptly dropped the case.
sentences.zh: 但随后，检察官突然撤诉了。

sentences.en: Kim wanted to know why.
sentences.zh: 金想知道原因。

sentences.en: She chronicles her reinvestigation of the case over eight episodes.
sentences.zh: 她通过八集节目记录了自己对这起案件的重新调查。

sentences.en: Take a listen to episode one.
sentences.zh: 请听第一集。

sentences.en: Years ago, when I was a teenager, I lived in Laramie, Wyoming.
sentences.zh: 多年前，我还是个十几岁的少年时，住在怀俄明州的拉勒米。

sentences.en: I've always remembered it as a mean town.
sentences.zh: 我一直记得那是个刻薄的小镇。

sentences.en: Uncommonly mean.
sentences.zh: 不同寻常的刻薄。

sentences.en: A place of jagged edges and cold people.
sentences.zh: 一个充满棱角、人情冷漠的地方。

sentences.en: Where the wind blew so hard, it actually whipped pebbles at you.
sentences.zh: 那里的风吹得如此猛烈，甚至会把小石子吹得打在你身上。

sentences.en: Actually pushed trucks off the highway.
sentences.zh: 甚至能把卡车从公路上吹翻。

sentences.en: Laramie stood at an elevation of more than 7,000 feet and got so socked in by winter storms, it felt like we were trapped.
sentences.zh: 拉勒米海拔超过7000英尺，冬季暴风雪封城时，感觉我们就像被困住了一样。

sentences.en: Like there was no way out.
sentences.zh: 就像无处可逃。

sentences.en: My family moved away before my senior year in high school.
sentences.zh: 我高三那年之前，全家搬走了。

sentences.en: I never wanted to go back.
sentences.zh: 我从没想过要回去。

sentences.en: The town's only high school, Laramie High, was grim even by normal high school standards.
sentences.zh: 镇上唯一的高中——拉勒米高中，即便以普通高中的标准来看，也显得阴森压抑。

sentences.en: One of my classmates killed someone.
sentences.zh: 我的同学里有人杀了人。

sentences.en: Other students killed themselves.
sentences.zh: 还有学生自杀了。

sentences.en: Some boys were held down and branded with letters, like they were livestock.
sentences.zh: 有些男生被按住，像牲口一样被烙上了字母。

sentences.en: Coaches who caught guys fighting in the hallways made them fight for real, in a makeshift ring.
sentences.zh: 教练如果发现学生在走廊打架，就会让他们在一个临时搭建的拳击台里真打。

sentences.en: Laramie wanted to raise its men as macho cowboys.
sentences.zh: 拉勒米想把男孩子们培养成大男子主义的牛仔。

sentences.en: Weakness wasn't tolerated.
sentences.zh: 这里容不下软弱。

sentences.en: And the girls had to look a certain way, act a certain way, wear a certain kind of eyeliner, have a certain kind of bi-level haircut.
sentences.zh: 女孩子们必须有特定的样子，特定的举止，画特定的眼线，留特定的双层发型。

sentences.en: I was bullied for the way I spoke, the way I dressed.
sentences.zh: 我因为说话和穿衣的方式而遭到霸凌。

sentences.en: I can still hear some boys mock-barking my name,
sentences.zh: 我至今还能听到一些男生在走廊里模仿狗叫着我的名字，

sentences.en: Kim Barker, down the hallway.
sentences.zh: “金·巴克”，在走廊里回荡。

sentences.en: Whenever I'd talk about the roughest place I'd ever lived,
sentences.zh: 每当我谈起我住过的最艰苦的地方时，

sentences.en: I'd always say Laramie.
sentences.zh: 我总是说是拉勒米。

sentences.en: Not Kabul, even though I reported there from the middle of a war.
sentences.zh: 不是喀布尔，尽管我曾在战火纷飞中在那里做过报道。

sentences.en: Not Islamabad, even though suicide bombs exploded there regularly.
sentences.zh: 也不是伊斯兰堡，尽管那里经常发生自杀式炸弹袭击。

sentences.en: There's a good chance that if you've heard of Laramie before, it's because of Matthew Shepard, a gay university student who was tortured there, and later died.
sentences.zh: 如果你以前听说过拉勒米，很有可能是因为马修·谢巴德，一名在那里被折磨致死的同性恋大学生。

sentences.en: When I first heard about his death, I thought, of course that happened in Laramie.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次听说他的死讯时，我想，这事发生在拉勒米一点也不奇怪。

sentences.en: But the main reason that Laramie has always stuck with me, the defining cruelty in a litany of him, was a young woman I had never met, named Shelly Wiley.
sentences.zh: 但拉勒米一直萦绕在我心头的根本原因，那连串残酷事件中最具代表性的一桩，是一位我从未谋面的年轻女性，名叫雪莉·威利。

sentences.en: In the fall of 1985, when I was a high school sophomore,
sentences.zh: 1985年秋天，我上高二时，

sentences.en: Shelly was murdered in her apartment.
sentences.zh: 雪莉在她的公寓里被谋杀了。

sentences.en: She was a few years older than me and had gone to Laramie High.
sentences.zh: 她比我大几岁，也上过拉勒米高中。

sentences.en: She went to college at the nearby University of Wyoming and earned money waiting tables at a truck stop.
sentences.zh: 她在附近的怀俄明大学上学，靠在卡车休息站当服务员赚取生活费。

sentences.en: She was 22, white, a pretty brunette, living a version of the life me and my friends imagined for ourselves one day.
sentences.zh: 她22岁，白人，漂亮的棕发女孩，过着我和朋友们想象中未来生活的一个版本。

sentences.en: The details of her death were less clear to me at 14 than the brutality was.
sentences.zh: 14岁时，我对她死因细节的了解远不如对那种残暴感的认知深刻。

sentences.en: There were whispers about stabbings and blood.
sentences.zh: 当时有关于刺伤和血迹的传言。

sentences.en: I'd heard that whoever had killed Shelly had burned her apartment to the ground.
sentences.zh: 我听说杀害雪莉的人把她的公寓烧成了平地。

sentences.en: I remember the shock of her murder arriving at my high school.
sentences.zh: 我记得她遇害的消息传到我们高中时，那种震惊感。

sentences.en: Some students became suspects.
sentences.zh: 有些学生成了嫌疑人。

sentences.en: Others played the guessing game.
sentences.zh: 其他人则玩起了猜谜游戏。

sentences.en: In one particularly terrifying round of Ouija with friends, we asked for a sign if the spirit knew who killed Shelly Wiley.
sentences.zh: 在一次特别恐怖的通灵板游戏中，我们问如果灵魂知道是谁杀了雪莉·威利，就给个信号。

sentences.en: At that very moment, a knock came on the basement window.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，地下室的窗户被敲响了。

sentences.en: Even the boys screamed.
sentences.zh: 连男生们都尖叫起来。

sentences.en: Shelly's murder was never solved.
sentences.zh: 雪莉的谋杀案一直没能破获。

sentences.en: Every few years, after I moved away, after I became a reporter,
sentences.zh: 我搬走并成为记者后的每隔几年，

sentences.en: I'd search her name for news, almost as an idle reflex.
sentences.zh: 我都会像一种无意识的条件反射一样，搜索她的名字看有没有新闻。

sentences.en: There was never anything.
sentences.zh: 但什么都没有。

sentences.en: Then came January 2021.
sentences.zh: 直到2021年1月。

sentences.en: I was cooped up in my apartment.
sentences.zh: 我被关在公寓里。

sentences.en: Just me, my dog Lucy, and a global pandemic.
sentences.zh: 只有我和我的狗露西，还有一场全球大流行。

sentences.en: Like almost everyone else, I was going a little bit stir-crazy.
sentences.zh: 和几乎所有人一样，我快要疯了。

sentences.en: I also owed my newspaper some story ideas, and, truthfully, I was tapped out.
sentences.zh: 我还欠报社一些选题，说实话，我灵感枯竭了。

sentences.en: So with a special kind of desperation,
sentences.zh: 所以带着一种特别的绝望，

sentences.en: I googled Shelly's name again.
sentences.zh: 我又谷歌搜索了雪莉的名字。

sentences.en: This time, there was news.
sentences.zh: 这一次，有新闻了。

sentences.en: 31 years after Shelly's murder, the police had actually made an arrest in the case.
sentences.zh: 在雪莉遇害31年后，警方竟然真的逮捕了一名嫌疑人。

sentences.en: A guy named Fred Lamb.
sentences.zh: 一个叫弗雷德·兰姆的家伙。

sentences.en: He was a one-time cop, a former sheriff's deputy and Laramie police officer.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一名警察，当过警长副手和拉勒米警官。

sentences.en: According to news reports, on the night Shelly was killed in 1985,
sentences.zh: 据新闻报道，1985年雪莉遇害的那晚，

sentences.en: Fred Lamb had been staying in the apartment two doors down from her.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德·兰姆就住在离她两个门远的公寓里。

sentences.en: His blood had been found at the scene.
sentences.zh: 现场发现了他的血迹。

sentences.en: And, after being confronted with DNA evidence in 2016, he had even told police that, quote,
sentences.zh: 而且，在2016年面对DNA证据时，他甚至告诉警方，引用原话：

sentences.en: I'm not denying that I did it.
sentences.zh: “我不否认是我干的。”

sentences.en: And,
sentences.zh: 而且，

sentences.en: Fred Lamb did it.
sentences.zh: “弗雷德·兰姆干的。”

sentences.en: But then, a few months after charging him,
sentences.zh: 但随后，在对他提起指控几个月后，

sentences.en: prosecutors unexpectedly dropped the case.
sentences.zh: 检察官出人意料地撤销了案件。

sentences.en: An article in the local paper headlined,
sentences.zh: 当地报纸的一篇文章标题是：

sentences.en: Possible Delay in Cold Case, quoted the prosecutor, who said her office needed more time to get test results back.
sentences.zh: 《悬案可能延期》，文中引用了检察官的话，她说办公室需要更多时间来获取检测结果。

sentences.en: She said they were dropping the charges against Fred, but only temporarily.
sentences.zh: 她说他们撤销对弗雷德的指控只是暂时的。

sentences.en: They planned to refile soon.
sentences.zh: 他们计划很快重新起诉。

sentences.en: That was in early 2017.
sentences.zh: 那是2017年初的事了。

sentences.en: To this day, prosecutors haven't refiled.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，检察官也没有重新起诉。

sentences.en: Which means, a former cop had been arrested.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，一名曾经的警察被捕了。

sentences.en: His DNA had been found at the scene.
sentences.zh: 现场发现了他的DNA。

sentences.en: He'd even, apparently, given something like a confession.
sentences.zh: 他甚至显然做出过类似认罪的陈述。

sentences.en: And then, nothing?
sentences.zh: 然后，就没下文了？

sentences.en: The whole thing seemed so Laramie.
sentences.zh: 这一切看起来太“拉勒米”了。

sentences.en: I doubted this was a story my editor would be into.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑我的编辑会对这个故事感兴趣。

sentences.en: A random 36-year-old cold case from my time in high school that might have a perfectly reasonable explanation for where it stood.
sentences.zh: 一个36年前的随机悬案，发生在我高中时期，而且可能对现状有一个完全合理的解释。

sentences.en: But I decided to make some calls anyway.
sentences.zh: 但我还是决定打几个电话试试。

sentences.en: Pull some string.
sentences.zh: 找找线索。

sentences.en: I figured, what's the harm in a little side project?
sentences.zh: 我想，做一个小小的副业有什么坏处呢？

sentences.en: From Serial Productions in the New York Times,
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》Serial Productions制作，

sentences.en: I'm Kim Barker.
sentences.zh: 我是金·巴克。

sentences.en: This is The Coldest Case in Laramie.
sentences.zh: 这是《拉勒米最冷悬案》。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的“Connections”拼图游戏。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天负责制作“Spelling Bee”和“Letterboxd”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫“联觉”的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的人们制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏吧。

sentences.en: I read through the handful of articles about Fred Lamb I could find on the internet.
sentences.zh: 我读遍了网上能找到的关于弗雷德·兰姆的几篇文章。

sentences.en: And then I started looking for Shelley's family.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始寻找雪莉的家人。

sentences.en: I didn't find much.
sentences.zh: 没找到太多信息。

sentences.en: An obit for Shelley's father.
sentences.zh: 一份雪莉父亲的讣告。

sentences.en: And a pleading Facebook post from a young woman named Brandy saying she was Shelley Wiley's niece.
sentences.zh: 还有一位叫布兰迪的年轻女性在Facebook上发的求助帖，说她是雪莉·威利的侄女。

sentences.en: She didn't name Lamb, but she said a former sheriff's deputy, a quote, monster, had never had to answer for his crime.
sentences.zh: 她没有点名兰姆，但她说一位前警长副手，一个“怪物”，从未为他的罪行负责。

sentences.en: Brandy said that she and her family needed help.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪说她和家人需要帮助。

sentences.en: I messaged her.
sentences.zh: 我给她发了信息。

sentences.en: We set up a time to Zoom, along with her mom, Lori,
sentences.zh: 我们约好和她妈妈洛里一起进行Zoom通话，

sentences.en: Shelley Wiley's younger sister.
sentences.zh: 洛里是雪莉·威利的妹妹。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Can you hear me?
sentences.zh: 能听到我说话吗？

sentences.en: Yes, can you hear me?
sentences.zh: 可以，你能听到我吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm just moving over to the Zoom.
sentences.zh: 可以，我刚转到Zoom这边。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: You must be Lori.
sentences.zh: 你一定是洛里吧。

sentences.en: I am.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Good to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: I'm obviously, and I'm obviously Kim, and that's, oh, hi, Brandy.
sentences.zh: 我显然是，我显然是金，那位是，哦，嗨，布兰迪。

sentences.en: Good to see you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: So, like, I figured we should start out with you guys asking me questions about what I'm doing, and like, you know, I would imagine that you would have questions.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想我们应该先从你们问我关于我在做什么的问题开始，我想你们肯定会有疑问。

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: What are you writing about exactly?
sentences.zh: 你到底在写什么？

sentences.en: So, what I would be interested in doing is basically trying to find out what happened with the case against Fred Lamb.
sentences.zh: 我感兴趣的是，基本上是想弄清楚针对弗雷德·兰姆的案件到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: like, just get records, do all the sort of things that you do.
sentences.zh: 比如，获取记录，做所有你们会做的那类事情。

sentences.en: I just, I feel like that there could be something there, especially given, like,
sentences.zh: 我只是，我觉得那儿可能有什么线索，尤其是考虑到，比如，

sentences.en: Fred Lamb was a cop.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德·兰姆曾是一名警察。

sentences.en: Oh, there is something there,
sentences.zh: 哦，那儿确实有线索，

sentences.en: I'm sure.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定。

sentences.en: I'd hesitated before reaching out to Lori directly.
sentences.zh: 我之前一直犹豫要不要直接联系洛莉。

sentences.en: For one thing, I could see from LinkedIn that she was the director of nursing at a nursing home in California in the middle of a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 首先，我从领英上看到，她当时正身处疫情中心，在加州一家养老院担任护理主任。

sentences.en: I figured she was busy.
sentences.zh: 我想她肯定很忙。

sentences.en: I didn't want to do this story without talking to her, and I knew my call could open up old wounds.
sentences.zh: 在没和她谈过之前，我不想做这个报道，而且我知道我的电话可能会揭开旧伤疤。

sentences.en: But Lori was blunt and matter-of-fact and willing to talk.
sentences.zh: 但洛莉说话直截了当、实事求是，而且愿意交谈。

sentences.en: So, why don't we start with what your understanding is with what happened with Fred Lamb?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们先从你对弗雷德·兰姆案的了解开始谈起，好吗？

sentences.en: So, what happened with Fred Lamb is, well, like, when they arrested him a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 关于弗雷德·兰姆，是这样的，嗯，比如，几年前他们逮捕他的时候。

sentences.en: I know it's very political, and I know they had to keep things a secret from a lot of people in the police department at the time.
sentences.zh: 我知道这事儿政治性很强，也知道当时警察局里的人不得不对很多人保密。

sentences.en: But I did sit down with them about,
sentences.zh: 但我确实和他们坐下来谈过，

sentences.en: I'm going to say, three, four years ago and looked at most of the case with them.
sentences.zh: 我想大概是三四年前吧，和他们一起看了大部分案卷。

sentences.en: Well, not most of the case.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也不算大部分案卷。

sentences.en: I was there for like three hours and looked at a lot of it.
sentences.zh: 我在那儿待了大概三个小时，看了很多内容。

sentences.en: And what did you see?
sentences.zh: 那你看到了什么？

sentences.en: Like, what did they show you?
sentences.zh: 比如，他们给你看了什么？

sentences.en: Oh, good Lord, it's a long story.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，说来话长。

sentences.en: But when we went in, so,
sentences.zh: 但当我们进去的时候，所以，

sentences.en: I went to Laramie, and actually,
sentences.zh: 我去了拉勒米，其实，

sentences.en: I'm really good friends with my sister's roommate at the time,
sentences.zh: 我和我姐姐当时的室友关系非常好，

sentences.en: Michelle.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔。

sentences.en: Oh, I would love to talk to her.
sentences.zh: 哦，我很想和她谈谈。

sentences.en: I'd seen mentions of Shelly's roommate,
sentences.zh: 我在卡斯珀报纸的一篇旧报道中看到过提到雪莉的室友，

sentences.en: Michelle, in an old news story in the Casper paper.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔。

sentences.en: In the few articles I could find online,
sentences.zh: 在我能在网上找到的为数不多的文章里，

sentences.en: Michelle was the only person quoted who actually knew Shelly, the only friend mentioned.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔是唯一被引用且真正认识雪莉的人，也是唯一被提到的朋友。

sentences.en: I'm sure Michelle would probably talk to you too.
sentences.zh: 我相信米歇尔可能也会愿意和你谈谈。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, actually,
sentences.zh: 所以，其实，

sentences.en: Michelle, I hadn't seen her in a long time, but I had flown from my dad's house, and Michelle picked me up, but we drove to Laramie, and she'd already talked to him,
sentences.zh: 米歇尔，我很久没见她了，但我从我爸家飞过去，米歇尔接了我，我们开车去了拉勒米，她已经和他谈过了，

sentences.en: but I went there, and I talked to the detective.
sentences.zh: 但我去了那里，和那位侦探谈了谈。

sentences.en: We were in the room, and I know somebody was on the camera watching or guiding him.
sentences.zh: 我们在房间里，我知道有人在摄像头后面看着或者在指导他。

sentences.en: I could tell.
sentences.zh: 我看得出来。

sentences.en: But they just went over the story, and they basically said, so, so his apartment was two apartments down.
sentences.zh: 但他们只是过了一遍案情，基本上他们说，所以，他的公寓就在两户之外。

sentences.en: The basics, as I understood them from talking to Lori and reading about
sentences.zh: 根据我与洛莉交谈以及阅读相关资料所了解到的基本情况，

sentences.en: Fred Lamb's arreSt.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德·兰姆被捕了。

sentences.en: Back in 1985, he had just left the sheriff's department and joined the National Guard full-time, married with a kid living just outside of Laramie.
sentences.zh: 1985年，他刚离开治安官办公室，全职加入了国民警卫队，已婚并育有一子，住在拉勒米郊外。

sentences.en: But on guard drill weekends, he stayed at his friend's place in town, which happened to be in the same apartment building as Shelly and Michelle, just two doors down.
sentences.zh: 但在警卫队训练的周末，他会住在城里朋友的住处，恰好就在雪莉和米歇尔住的那栋公寓楼里，只隔了两扇门。

sentences.en: The weekend of Shelly's murder was a drill weekend, so Fred was staying over as usual.
sentences.zh: 雪莉遇害的那个周末正好是训练周末，所以弗雷德像往常一样住在那里。

sentences.en: Lori told me the last time she saw her sister,
sentences.zh: 洛莉告诉我，她最后一次见到她姐姐，

sentences.en: Shelly, was just a few hours before she was killed.
sentences.zh: 雪莉，是在她遇害前几个小时。

sentences.en: Shelly and a girlfriend had spent the evening talking and drinking tea in her living room.
sentences.zh: 雪莉和一个女性朋友在客厅里聊天喝茶度过了一晚。

sentences.en: Lori stopped by after getting off of work, but soon Shelly sent Lori and her friend home.
sentences.zh: 洛莉下班后顺道过来，但没过多久，雪莉就让洛莉和她朋友回家了。

sentences.en: Shelly had to get up early for her waitressing shift.
sentences.zh: 雪莉第二天要早起去当服务员。

sentences.en: Michelle was gone for the night, so Shelly was alone.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔那天晚上不在，所以雪莉一个人在家。

sentences.en: At some point in the early morning hours of Sunday,
sentences.zh: 周日凌晨的某个时候，

sentences.en: October 20th, someone got inside of Shelly's apartment and attacked her in her bedroom.
sentences.zh: 10月20日，有人闯进了雪莉的公寓，在卧室里袭击了她。

sentences.en: It looked like she'd tried to escape.
sentences.zh: 看起来她试图逃跑。

sentences.en: She made it out the front door.
sentences.zh: 她逃到了前门外。

sentences.en: But on the sidewalk just outside of her building, her attacker caught her, stabbed her repeatedly,
sentences.zh: 但在楼外的人行道上，袭击者抓住了她，反复刺伤她，

sentences.en: dragged Shelly back inside before setting the apartment on fire.
sentences.zh: 把雪莉拖回屋内，然后放火烧了公寓。

sentences.en: At about 5.20 in the morning, witnesses saw flames shooting out of Shelly's apartment, engulfing the living room and the front door.
sentences.zh: 凌晨5点20分左右，目击者看到火焰从雪莉的公寓喷涌而出，吞噬了客厅和前门。

sentences.en: Fred was there, one of the few people at the scene.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德当时就在现场，是现场为数不多的人之一。

sentences.en: Police interviewed Fred late that afternoon.
sentences.zh: 警方在当天下午晚些时候审问了弗雷德。

sentences.en: He told them he had guard duty the next day and would be heading to Arkansas for a couple weeks of training.
sentences.zh: 他告诉他们，他第二天有值勤任务，要去阿肯色州进行为期两周的训练。

sentences.en: And then, as far as Lori knew, the cops never looked at Fred again.
sentences.zh: 然后，据洛莉所知，警察再也没有调查过弗雷德。

sentences.en: Not until three decades later, in 2016, when Laramie investigators keyed in on Fred for the murder.
sentences.zh: 直到三十年后，2016年，拉勒米的调查人员才重新锁定弗雷德为谋杀嫌疑人。

sentences.en: They gathered evidence and called Fred in for an interview.
sentences.zh: 他们收集了证据，并传唤弗雷德进行审讯。

sentences.en: This one lasted more than seven hours.
sentences.zh: 这次审讯持续了七个多小时。

sentences.en: Near the end, according to news reports, is when Fred referred to himself in the third person and said things such as,
sentences.zh: 据新闻报道，在审讯快结束时，弗雷德开始用第三人称指代自己，并说了诸如，

sentences.en: Fred Lamb did it and, bottom line is,
sentences.zh: 弗雷德·兰姆干的，底线是，

sentences.en: I killed a girl.
sentences.zh: 我杀了一个女孩。

sentences.en: After Fred was charged,
sentences.zh: 在弗雷德被起诉后，

sentences.en: Lori said the lead detective brought in her and Michelle and walked them through the early mistakes in the case.
sentences.zh: 洛莉说，首席侦探把她和米歇尔叫去，向她们详细说明了案件早期的失误。

sentences.en: Because I asked the detective,
sentences.zh: 因为我问过侦探，

sentences.en: I'm like, well, why did the crime scene tape only go to the first department?
sentences.zh: 我说，为什么警戒线只拉到了第一间公寓？

sentences.en: And when he looked at the picture, sure enough, they didn't even go to the second or third apartment, even though there was more evidence further down.
sentences.zh: 当他看照片时，果然，他们甚至没去第二或第三间公寓，尽管更远的地方还有更多证据。

sentences.en: So anyhow, yeah, they let Fred go, but there was, he did have some blood spatter on his door.
sentences.zh: 总之，是的，他们放走了弗雷德，但他确实，他门上有血迹喷溅。

sentences.en: He had a cut on his hand and he said,
sentences.zh: 他手上有一道伤口，他说，

sentences.en: he cut his hand, I can't remember what he told them knocking on the door.
sentences.zh: 他弄伤了手，我不记得他告诉他们是在敲门时弄伤的还是什么。

sentences.en: I can't remember how he got that.
sentences.zh: 我不记得他是怎么弄伤的了。

sentences.en: But I know he went behind the building at one point, cut the whole phone line.
sentences.zh: 但我知道他有一次绕到楼后，剪断了整条电话线。

sentences.en: I mean, what's it like to find out they arrested a guy two doors down?
sentences.zh: 我是说，发现凶手就是隔两户的邻居，是什么感觉？

sentences.en: I think Michelle was like, I knew he may have had something to do with it.
sentences.zh: 我想米歇尔当时说，我知道他可能和这事有关。

sentences.en: Michelle said that from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔从一开始就这么说。

sentences.en: Um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: I don't know if she knew it was him, but she questioned.
sentences.zh: 我不知道她是否知道就是他，但她确实怀疑过。

sentences.en: Lori says they all knew
sentences.zh: 洛莉说他们都认识

sentences.en: Fred Lamb.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德·兰姆。

sentences.en: He used to go to Foster's, a huge truck stop off of Interstate 80, where Lori,
sentences.zh: 他以前常去福斯特餐厅，那是80号州际公路旁一个巨大的卡车休息站，洛莉、

sentences.en: Michelle, and Shelly all worked.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔和雪莉都在那儿工作。

sentences.en: They'd see Fred at Foster's, meeting with other cops to drink coffee and shoot the shit.
sentences.zh: 她们常在福斯特餐厅看到弗雷德，他和其他警察在那儿喝咖啡、闲聊。

sentences.en: Foster's was just across the dirt road from Shelly's apartment building.
sentences.zh: 福斯特餐厅就在雪莉公寓楼对面那条土路那边。

sentences.en: The building itself wasn't much.
sentences.zh: 那栋楼本身不怎么样。

sentences.en: Five low-slung units arranged in an L-shape.
sentences.zh: 五间低矮的单元房呈L型排列。

sentences.en: It was the kind of building that looks like a strip of crummy motel rooms, but is in fact a strip of crummy rental units along a sidewalk and parking lot.
sentences.zh: 那栋楼看起来就像一排破旧的汽车旅馆房间，但实际上是沿着人行道和停车场的一排破旧出租单元。

sentences.en: That's the other place
sentences.zh: 那是另一个地方，

sentences.en: Lori remembers seeing Fred sometimes, when she was over at Shelly's apartment building.
sentences.zh: 洛莉记得有时会看到弗雷德，当她去雪莉的公寓楼时。

sentences.en: We would sit outside, sometimes we'd sunbathe out there, because that's what you did in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 我们常坐在外面，有时在那儿晒太阳，因为80年代大家都是这么做的。

sentences.en: I know when they said it in the report,
sentences.zh: 我知道当他们在报告里提到这一点时，

sentences.en: I'm like, oh my god, you're trying to make us look like whores, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 我心想，天哪，你们是想把我们描绘成荡妇，对吧？

sentences.en: I pretty much told him that.
sentences.zh: 我几乎是直接对他这么说的。

sentences.en: I'm like, that's not how it was then, that's not really what we were.
sentences.zh: 我说，当时的情况不是那样的，我们也不是那样的人。

sentences.en: But they came home, but I remember I was, I don't even think we were sunbathing this time, but we were standing outside and I must have been leaving, but I remember
sentences.zh: 但他们回家了，我记得我当时，我觉得我们这次甚至没在晒太阳，但我们站在外面，我当时肯定是要走了，但我记得

sentences.en: Michelle smacking me and telling me, look at those weirdos, there's my neighbors, he's a weirdo.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔拍了我一下，告诉我，看那些怪人，那是我的邻居，他是个怪胎。

sentences.en: But I remember a couple weeks before their screen kept coming off their window, different screens,
sentences.zh: 但我记得在她们出事的前几周，她们窗户上的纱窗总是掉下来，不同的纱窗，

sentences.en: and somebody, they had somebody put it back on, or he offered to put it back on and Michelle turned him down one time, but I remember their screens in the front would come off
sentences.zh: 有人，她们找人装回去，或者他主动提出装回去，米歇尔有一次拒绝了他，但我记得前面的纱窗会掉下来，

sentences.en: and then in the back would come off, but they never knew who it was, they weren't too worried about it at the time.
sentences.zh: 然后后面的也会掉下来，但她们从不知道是谁干的，当时她们也没太在意。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What did you think about the fact that he was a former police officer and used to be in the sheriff?
sentences.zh: 对于他曾是警察且在治安官办公室工作过这件事，你怎么看？

sentences.en: Well, at first I had to realize I was like, hmm, I didn't have a lot of feelings either way, and then I'm like,
sentences.zh: 嗯，起初我得意识到，我当时想，嗯，我没什么特别的感觉，然后我想，

sentences.en: well, they're assholes because they wouldn't really answer any of our questions.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们就是混蛋，因为他们根本不回答我们的任何问题。

sentences.en: But yeah, I was pretty naive then,
sentences.zh: 但确实，我当时太天真了，

sentences.en: I'm not nearly as naive now or these days, you know, I would have hounded them or called them more, but yeah, no, they didn't tell us they had any suspects or that they really
sentences.zh: 我现在可没那么天真了，你知道，如果是在现在，我会缠着他们或者给他们打更多电话，但确实，不，他们没告诉我们有任何嫌疑人，也没说他们真的

sentences.en: talked to them or that I remember.
sentences.zh: 审问过他们，或者我记得是这样。

sentences.en: The detective who was in charge of it now is not somebody who was originally a police officer at the time.
sentences.zh: 现在负责此案的侦探并不是当时最初的警察之一。

sentences.en: He's not from Laramie.
sentences.zh: 他不是拉勒米本地人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, so he's like, he's not familiar with the case.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以他就像，他对这个案子不熟悉。

sentences.en: I'm now sitting inside my bathroom because my dog's being super loud.
sentences.zh: 我现在坐在浴室里，因为我的狗叫得太厉害了。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的。

sentences.en: Jeff, you can move inside here.
sentences.zh: 杰夫，你可以进来。

sentences.en: He's familiar with the case.
sentences.zh: 他熟悉这个案子。

sentences.en: He ended up with the case and he investigated and he's the one who got the warrant to arrest Brad the first time.
sentences.zh: 他最终接手了这个案子并进行了调查，是他第一次拿到逮捕布拉德的搜查令。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And then
sentences.zh: 然后

sentences.en: I don't know, he's now like the assistant chief of police, but he kept the case.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，他现在好像是助理警察局长，但他保留了这个案子。

sentences.en: So he sounds like he's very invested in it then.
sentences.zh: 听起来他在这案子上投入了很多精力。

sentences.en: He's very invested in it.
sentences.zh: 他投入了很多精力。

sentences.en: He's the only one that'll help me with anything.
sentences.zh: 他是唯一一个会在任何事情上帮助我的人。

sentences.en: Nobody else will go further.
sentences.zh: 没别人愿意再深入了。

sentences.en: He's the only one that tries to get them to press charges or to move forward or to do any of that.
sentences.zh: 他是唯一一个试图让他们提起诉讼、推动案件进展或做任何这些事情的人。

sentences.en: Nobody else will really help.
sentences.zh: 没别人会真正帮忙。

sentences.en: And what's his name?
sentences.zh: 他叫什么名字？

sentences.en: The deputy?
sentences.zh: 那位副局长？

sentences.en: Uh, the detective or that he's maybe the, I'm not even sure his title now.
sentences.zh: 呃，那位侦探，或者他可能是，我甚至不确定他现在的头衔。

sentences.en: The assistant chief, his name is Robert Terry.
sentences.zh: 那位助理局长，他叫罗伯特·特里。

sentences.en: Robert Terry.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·特里。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And how did you find out that they were going to drop the charges at least for now against slam?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么知道他们要撤销对兰姆的指控，至少是暂时撤销的？

sentences.en: I read it in paper.
sentences.zh: 我在报纸上读到的。

sentences.en: Ooh, they didn't call you and tell you.
sentences.zh: 哦，他们没打电话通知你吗？

sentences.en: Oh, no, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，没有，没有。

sentences.en: Anytime I call any of the attorneys, they have only had victims witness call me like twice.
sentences.zh: 每次我给律师打电话，他们只有两次让受害者证人给我回过电话。

sentences.en: I called a lot though.
sentences.zh: 不过我打了很多次电话。

sentences.en: I hounded the police station when he was arrested and the first police officer that answered at the jail house, um, she was really rude and she was like, I don't know
sentences.zh: 在他被捕时，我缠着警察局打听，监狱里接电话的第一个女警，嗯，她非常粗鲁，她说，我不知道

sentences.en: what case you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 你在说哪个案子。

sentences.en: So she transferred me to another police officer and he told me that he wasn't allowed to discuss the case.
sentences.zh: 所以她把我转接给了另一位警官，他告诉我他不被允许讨论这个案子。

sentences.en: But then it got really quiet and it was like he was whispering in the phone and he said, you need to pursue this.
sentences.zh: 但后来电话那头变得非常安静，就像他在电话里低声说，你需要继续追查这个案子。

sentences.en: Don't stop.
sentences.zh: 别停下。

sentences.en: And then he hung up the phone.
sentences.zh: 然后他就挂断了电话。

sentences.en: But at one point, um, Peggy Trent was the prosecutor for it
sentences.zh: 但有一次，嗯，佩吉·特伦特是负责此案的检察官，

sentences.en: and I called her a few times and she wouldn't answer the phone.
sentences.zh: 我给她打过几次电话，她都不接。

sentences.en: And then I kind of got on a kick of, you know, calling.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始有一种冲动，你知道，不停地打电话。

sentences.en: I thought in my head,
sentences.zh: 我在心里想，

sentences.en: I'm like, I feel like Laramie is really a bad place to try it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得拉勒米真的不是审理此案的好地方。

sentences.en: So I wonder if there's something that I could do, you know, or to get it transferred out of Laramie to maybe Cheyenne.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道我能不能做点什么，你知道，或者把案子从拉勒米转到夏延去。

sentences.en: So I remember calling Cheyenne and asking them, you know, if they knew about the case and that I was her niece and, um, how they get it transferred or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以我记得我给夏延打过电话，问他们，你知道，他们是否知道这个案子，我是受害者的侄女，嗯，他们怎么才能把案子转过去之类的。

sentences.en: And the lady that I spoke to, she said, I can't just, um, take the case.
sentences.zh: 和我通话的那位女士说，嗯，我不能直接接手这个案子。

sentences.en: She said, it has to be given to us by Peggy Trent.
sentences.zh: 她说，这案子必须由佩吉·特伦特（Peggy Trent）移交给我们才行。

sentences.en: But she was like, can I call you right back in 15 minutes?
sentences.zh: 但她又说，我能15分钟后再给你回电话吗？

sentences.en: And I'm like, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我说，行啊。

sentences.en: And I didn't think she was going to call me back.
sentences.zh: 我当时以为她不会再打给我了。

sentences.en: Well, she called me back really quickly and she was like, yeah, I just spoke to a judge and we're, we want it, but we can't just take it.
sentences.zh: 结果，她很快就回了电话，说她刚和一位法官谈过，我们想要这个案子，但不能直接接手。

sentences.en: So I called
sentences.zh: 所以我给

sentences.en: Peggy Trent back and I told her, you know, like Cheyenne wants it in the case and I feel like it would be better to be, you know, tried outside of Laramie and she was so
sentences.zh: 佩吉·特伦特打了回去，告诉她，夏延市（Cheyenne）那边想要接手这个案子，我觉得在拉勒米（Laramie）之外审理会更好，她当时

sentences.en: angry with me.
sentences.zh: 非常生气。

sentences.en: She told me, um, how, who do you think you are just trying to take my case away?
sentences.zh: 她对我说，你以为你是谁啊，居然想把我的案子抢走？

sentences.en: So I was really frustrated with her and I would call her office every day, you know, just to ask questions.
sentences.zh: 我当时对她非常失望，于是每天都给她的办公室打电话，就是为了问些问题。

sentences.en: And eventually
sentences.zh: 最终，

sentences.en: I was sharing on my Facebook um, the article, you know, and saying this is my aunt, everybody please share.
sentences.zh: 我在Facebook上分享了那篇文章，说这是我的阿姨，请大家帮忙转发。

sentences.en: So, um, it started to get, you know, around a little bit and then Peggy Trent called my grandmother
sentences.zh: 事情开始传开了，然后佩吉·特伦特就给我祖母

sentences.en: on me and told my grandma that I was jeopardizing the case and to make me stop.
sentences.zh: 打了电话，告我的状，说我在破坏案子，让我住手。

sentences.en: She called my grandma on me.
sentences.zh: 她居然为了这事给我祖母打电话。

sentences.en: I talked to Peggy Trent about this story.
sentences.zh: 我曾就这件事和佩吉·特伦特谈过。

sentences.en: She told me she didn't remember
sentences.zh: 她说她不记得

sentences.en: Brandy calling her office nor did she remember calling Brandy's grandma.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪（Brandy）给她的办公室打过电话，也不记得给布兰迪的祖母打过电话。

sentences.en: Peggy has since left the prosecutor's office.
sentences.zh: 佩吉后来已经离开了检察官办公室。

sentences.en: She told me she wouldn't talk about an open investigation.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，她不会谈论正在进行的调查。

sentences.en: Lori graduated high school a few months before Shelly was killed.
sentences.zh: 洛里（Lori）在雪莉（Shelly）遇害前几个月刚高中毕业。

sentences.en: She told me she spent much of her time at Shelly's, even spent the night there sometimes.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，她大部分时间都待在雪莉家，有时甚至会过夜。

sentences.en: They were four years apart but Lori told me they were really close.
sentences.zh: 她们相差四岁，但洛里说她们关系非常亲密。

sentences.en: They drank beer, went to university football games.
sentences.zh: 她们一起喝啤酒，去看大学橄榄球比赛。

sentences.en: In a Garfield notebook they kept on
sentences.zh: 她们有一个加菲猫笔记本，放在

sentences.en: Shelly's dresser.
sentences.zh: 雪莉的梳妆台上。

sentences.en: They wrote about their lives from the perspective of a cat.
sentences.zh: 她们以猫的视角记录着自己的生活。

sentences.en: When Lori spoke to me about Shelly she did it without a lot of sentimentality.
sentences.zh: 当洛里跟我谈起雪莉时，并没有表现出太多的伤感。

sentences.en: She seemed like she put her memories of her sister and what happened into a box that she never opened.
sentences.zh: 她似乎把关于姐姐的记忆和发生的一切都锁进了一个从不打开的盒子里。

sentences.en: Kept a charm bracelet of Shelly's with a dangling ballerina in a bag in a drawer where she rarely saw it.
sentences.zh: 她把雪莉的一条挂着芭蕾舞女演员坠饰的手链放在抽屉里的袋子里，几乎从不去看。

sentences.en: Lori told me that Shelly's death devastated her family.
sentences.zh: 洛里告诉我，雪莉的死摧毁了她的家庭。

sentences.en: For Vicki,
sentences.zh: 对于维基（Vicki）来说，

sentences.en: Shelly's mom, the murder of her oldest child became the divider of life into before and after.
sentences.zh: 也就是雪莉的母亲，长女的遇害成了她人生中“之前”与“之后”的分水岭。

sentences.en: Life before.
sentences.zh: 生活在之前。

sentences.en: Vicki gave birth to Shelly just after high school and the two pretty much grew up together.
sentences.zh: 维基高中毕业后不久就生下了雪莉，两人几乎是一起长大的。

sentences.en: They looked alike, like sisters even.
sentences.zh: 她们长得很像，甚至像姐妹一样。

sentences.en: Talked all the time, even after Shelly's dad and Vicki divorced.
sentences.zh: 即使在雪莉的父亲和维基离婚后，她们也经常聊天。

sentences.en: Life after,
sentences.zh: 生活在之后，

sentences.en: Vicki became more of a recluse according to Lori, more depressed, more off on her own.
sentences.zh: 据洛里说，维基变得更加孤僻，更加抑郁，更加独来独往。

sentences.en: Shelly's dad kind of disappeared after his daughter's murder.
sentences.zh: 雪莉的父亲在女儿遇害后就消失了。

sentences.en: Spent much of his time alone in the mountains.
sentences.zh: 他大部分时间都独自待在山里。

sentences.en: Didn't want to talk about Shelly's murder.
sentences.zh: 不想谈论雪莉的谋杀案。

sentences.en: Didn't talk much about her at all.
sentences.zh: 几乎从不提起她。

sentences.en: He seemed to walk away from his second marriage without actually leaving.
sentences.zh: 他似乎在没有真正离开的情况下，就退出了他的第二次婚姻。

sentences.en: And after the couple finally broke up,
sentences.zh: 而在两人最终分手后，

sentences.en: Shelly's father left Laramie for good.
sentences.zh: 雪莉的父亲永远离开了拉勒米。

sentences.en: He died alone in Buffalo, Wyoming, leaving behind
sentences.zh: 他独自死在怀俄明州的布法罗（Buffalo），留下了一张

sentences.en: Shelly's funeral notice tucked inside a book and a bitter hatred of the Laramie police.
sentences.zh: 夹在书里的雪莉的葬礼通知，以及对拉勒米警方的刻骨仇恨。

sentences.en: One of Shelly's brothers started drinking after Shelly's death.
sentences.zh: 雪莉的一个兄弟在雪莉死后开始酗酒。

sentences.en: He never stopped.
sentences.zh: 他从未停止过。

sentences.en: He died shortly before my first conversation with Lori and Brandy.
sentences.zh: 他在我与洛里和布兰迪第一次谈话前不久去世了。

sentences.en: When I asked Shelly's family about her, what she was like, who she was, they tended to lean on the platitudes of the long dead.
sentences.zh: 当我问及雪莉的家人她是个什么样的人时，他们往往会用那些陈词滥调来形容逝者。

sentences.en: She lit up a room with her smile.
sentences.zh: 她的笑容照亮了整个房间。

sentences.en: She was smart, beautiful, inside and out.
sentences.zh: 她聪明、美丽，内外兼修。

sentences.en: And it makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这也很正常。

sentences.en: Shelly is, in their minds, forever 22.
sentences.zh: 在他们心中，雪莉永远是22岁。

sentences.en: A pretty woman who liked John Denver, who loved animals, especially cats, who worked out at the gym regularly before that was really a thing for women.
sentences.zh: 一个喜欢约翰·丹佛（John Denver）、热爱动物（尤其是猫）的漂亮女人，在女性健身还不流行的时候，她就已经经常去健身房锻炼了。

sentences.en: Who was often, in fact, the only woman in any of her engineering or industrial management classes.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她经常是工程或工业管理课上唯一的女性。

sentences.en: In truth, the most important parts of who Shelly Wiley was were still in the process of being ironed out.
sentences.zh: 说实话，雪莉·威利（Shelly Wiley）身上最重要的部分，其实还在塑造之中。

sentences.en: Her family mourns this just as much as they mourn the person they loved.
sentences.zh: 她的家人为此感到悲痛，就像他们哀悼那个他们深爱的人一样。

sentences.en: That she was murdered right at that precipice before she or anyone else had a chance to find out who she was going to be.
sentences.zh: 她就在那个关键时刻被谋杀了，还没来得及让她自己或任何人发现她未来会成为什么样的人。

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: I've talked to you guys for, like, more than an hour this evening.
sentences.zh: 今晚我和你们聊了一个多小时了。

sentences.en: I don't want to be, take too much of your time up in the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 我不想在刚开始就占用你们太多时间。

sentences.en: But, like, and I hate to say that I'm giving homework, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，我不想说我在布置家庭作业，对吧？

sentences.en: But, like, there's homework here.
sentences.zh: 但确实有作业要做。

sentences.en: If you guys could get me, like, if you could talk to Michelle and see if she'd talk to me.
sentences.zh: 如果你们能帮我联系一下米歇尔（Michelle），看看她愿不愿意跟我谈谈。

sentences.en: And I think that she would be really important to talk to just because he would be more familiar with what his role was in the building at the time and all that sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 我觉得和她谈谈非常重要，因为她会更了解当时他在大楼里的角色以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: I'm sure Michelle will talk to you.
sentences.zh: 我相信米歇尔会愿意和你们谈的。

sentences.en: That'd be great.
sentences.zh: 那太好了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 行。

sentences.en: And we'll just stay, just stay in touch.
sentences.zh: 我们会保持联系。

sentences.en: And we'll see where this can go, okay?
sentences.zh: 看看事情会有什么进展，好吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: What I gathered from talking to Lori and Brandy was that they didn't actually know a lot more about what happened with this case than what appeared in news reports.
sentences.zh: 从与洛里和布兰迪的谈话中，我了解到她们对这个案子其实并不比新闻报道里知道的多。

sentences.en: In that vacuum, they'd started developing some theories.
sentences.zh: 在这种信息真空下，她们开始产生了一些推测。

sentences.en: They were pretty clear that the whole thing was mishandled from the start, that Fred didn't get a close look as a suspect back in 1985.
sentences.zh: 她们很清楚，整个案子从一开始就处理不当，1985年时弗雷德（Fred）并没有被作为嫌疑人仔细调查。

sentences.en: They figured it was because he was a former cop, that maybe this was a good old boy as protecting their own thing.
sentences.zh: 她们认为这是因为他曾是警察，也许这就是那种官官相护的“老男孩”作风。

sentences.en: It was hard for Lori and Brandy to feel like there wasn't something shady going on here.
sentences.zh: 洛里和布兰迪很难不觉得这里面有什么猫腻。

sentences.en: They told me they'd be happy to have me find out what I could.
sentences.zh: 她们告诉我，如果我能查出些什么，她们会很高兴。

sentences.en: That's next time on The Coldest Case in Laramie.
sentences.zh: 下期《拉勒米最冷悬案》（The Coldest Case in Laramie）再见。

sentences.en: To hear the rest of the series, search for The Coldest Case in Laramie wherever you listen and subscribe.
sentences.zh: 想收听本系列节目的其余部分，请在您常用的播客平台搜索《拉勒米最冷悬案》并订阅。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们要为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们需要全黑的睡眠环境吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是累到昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求，因为这非常具体。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏或食物禁忌吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》App或您喜欢的任何平台上搜索《Wirecutter秀》。
